condition: mild postural lightheadedness on standing after antihypertensive dose increase
level_rationale: Feeling lightheaded upon standing 1 week after an antihypertensive dose increase with a mildly low-normal standing blood pressure of 106 over 66 today represents uncomplicated medication-related orthostatic lightheadedness warranting an outpatient doctor visit for dose review, whereas a standing blood pressure of 68 over 40 today indicates profound acute drug-induced hypotension requiring immediate ER evaluation.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Colloquial dialect lexicon swap ('lightheaded' vs 'swimmy headed', with 'my head feels swimmy' in everyday_paraphrase) + single-fact measured standing blood pressure escalation control (-cf, L2 to L4).

design_note: Uses four atomic facts (age 71, blood pressure pill dose increase 1 week ago, postural lightheadedness when standing up, and standing blood pressure 106 over 66 today) with a 10-word vs 12-word continuous span swap and 18 identical trailing tokens. Changing only the measured standing blood pressure value in atomic fact f4 from '106 over 66' to '68 over 40' obeys reviewer_notes.md Rule A first choice while shifting care from outpatient prescribing physician dose review (level 2) to acute hypotensive emergency care (level 4) with zero stated negatives.
